answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a non-transferable stake earned through attested work over time, like nectar gathered slowly, and slashing it if peers detect duplicate behavior. Newcomers start with low weight, similar to a willow sapling that must grow roots before shading others, gaining influence only after sustained attestations from diverse non-kin peers. Mass fabrication across a barren tundra of empty accounts then stays unprofitable because cost scales per identity while rewards do not.
